rv.q: An amusing indictment of our soul-crushing go-go-go ethos and a gleeful conjuring of community.
So run, yes run, don’t walk and get yourself a ticket to a show that will have you urging on others who are sweating buckets for your sole entertainment pleasure.
Wildly fun and unlike anything else on stage right now, Burnout Paradise is a singular theatre experience.
The show delivers a swift and agreeable serving of escapist entertainment and what’s wrong with that?
The effect of all this activity by audience and actors and host is deliberate chaos, made all the more so by some fancy, busy video, lighting and sound design.
It is chaotic, communal, and a genuine blast.
They’ve got a mission to accomplish: you’re either on board, or you’re useless.
Over time, I felt mostly exhausted by the sensory overload.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this high-energy Australian import, praising its inventive blend of physical endurance, interactive chaos, and spontaneous comedy as exhilarating entertainment that transforms modern burnout into theatrical spectacle.

vr.q: For my money, it is the most fun show in New York right now.
One of my favorite theater experiences is back in new york... it's just such a fun night. And the more you put into it, the more you will definitely get out of it.
Burnout Paradise is this delightfully insane piece of theatre slash performance art... you feel the sense of human connection and wanting to provide assistance and it's just so much fun.
You'll more likely than not be overstimulated, but in a good way.
